setting: You three all live in the same small village in County Galway, and you sit on the committee of its football club, which runs one adult team and a youth section from a pitch behind the primary school. You have known each other for years through the club and the village, so you're on first-name terms, and each of you knows roughly who handles what and who has opinions about the dressing-room rota.
opener: Asking Declan and Ciara whether the floodlight quote arrived before Friday's meeting.

Siobhan.knows: You know Declan as the treasurer who keeps the accounts in a cardboard folder and is never late with the figures. You know Ciara as the secretary who took over the minutes last year and is good with the grant forms.
Siobhan.like: You're brisk and organised with a dry sense of humour, and you care a lot about the club's reputation and getting decisions made properly. You tease Declan about his one-word replies and look out for Ciara, though you sometimes move too fast for her liking.
Siobhan.texts: You message in the chat fairly often, mostly to set agendas or chase people up.
Siobhan.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Declan.knows: You know Siobhan as the chair who runs meetings tightly and expects the agenda to be followed. You know Ciara as the secretary who is sharp with emails and copies everyone in.
Declan.like: You're dry and quiet with a deadpan sense of humour, you care about getting the numbers right, and you follow GAA and Premier League results closely. You tease Ciara about her long emails and quietly back Siobhan on decisions, though you get a bit irritated when things are settled by group chat.
Declan.texts: You message in the chat now and then, mostly when something needs a figure or a yes or no.
Declan.style: You type short messages with minimal punctuation and no emoji, though you send a thumbs-up now and then.

Ciara.knows: You know Siobhan as the chair you report to, who can be a bit formal. You know Declan as the treasurer who replies to emails in one line and thinks you over-explain.
Ciara.like: You're warm and quick, with a dry streak and strong opinions about the youth section, and you get enthusiastic about getting new kids playing. You look out for Siobhan and gently push back when she moves too fast, and you tease Declan about his one-word replies.
Ciara.texts: You message in the chat fairly often, usually to post fixtures or check something with the others.
Ciara.style: You type in full sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, and you use an emoji now and then.

private_lines.Siobhan: You live in a bungalow on the main road and run a small pharmacy in the village. This week you're chasing the council about the floodlights and getting ready for the AGM in December. Your daughter is coming home from Dublin on Friday for the weekend.
private_lines.Declan: You live in a semi-detached house on the far side of the village and work as an agricultural contractor, doing silage, hedge-cutting and haulage. This week the weather has kept you busy, and you have the club's bank statements to reconcile before the AGM.
private_lines.Ciara: You rent a cottage at the edge of the village and work remotely as a payroll administrator for a firm in Galway city, going in twice a week. This week you're finalising the spring fixtures and waiting on referee assignments.

situation: Three members of a village football club committee.

text: Did the floodlight quote come in? I need to know before Friday's meeting.
Not that I've seen. Checked the club email this afternoon, nothing from them.
nothing here
Right. I rang their office at four and got a machine. Will try again tomorrow.
Should I chase them by email or leave it to you?
Email them. Copy all of us. Ask for the quote in writing and a date.
Will do. Ciara here, not Siobhan, I know you know that 😂
Ciara, did the email go out?
Went at 9, no reply yet. Sent it to the council planning address too just in case.
Good. Declan, can you square the floodlight line in the accounts before Friday? Want the figure ready whatever they say.
will do
still no quote from them. bank rec about done
Fine. We'll go with what we have on Friday and flag it.
Did anyone hear from the council about the planning side? I'm going to bed soon so just checking before I go
Nothing. I'll ring them first thing. Declan, is the bank rec done or are we still waiting on that too?
nearly
one dodgy line from the september match day. cant find the cheque
Is it the gate money or the kit order?
kit order
Right. Don't spend the night on it. It can go in the AGM pack as an open item.
Hate open items. Ask Mick Heneghan, he paid for the kit himself in September I think, might have the receipt
ok

Also before I forget, I've drafted the spring fixtures. Can you both look over the youth Saturday slots? I've put the U12s on at 10 but the pitch booking says 11 on the sheet so one of us has it wrong
Ciara, I'll look tomorrow. I'm not sure I trust anything I read after nine tonight.
Fair. Bed for you then 😂
found it. mick paid cash. ill put the receipt in the folder
Good man. Thank you.
Morning. Ciara, I've rung the council. Planning office says the floodlight application is with an engineer and they'll have something by the end of the month. Nothing from the contractor yet.
Thanks Siobhan. I'll follow up with the contractor by email again today, copying everyone. Will check the fixtures against the pitch sheet this morning too.
any word on the referee for the 14th
Still waiting on the county board. Chased them yesterday.
Can we agree the AGM date today? I need to get the notices out this week.
the 11th is fine by me
Fine with me too. Shall I book the hall?
Yes please. Ciara, book it for seven.
Booked. Also the U12 slot was 11, my mistake. Corrected the draft.
Thank you.
got the receipt sorted for the kit order, also one of the sponsors short on his payment. ill sort it tomorrow
Did the contractor reply to anyone?
Not to me.
